Resolves #17958

The guide whose subject is extending a Neo class told a subclass author the opposite of what the engine enforces: a non-underscore property "is static and does not trigger this reactive behavior". For an override that is backwards — the bare name is the *only* legal spelling, it stays reactive, and repeating the underscore throws in `Neo.createConfig` (`src/Neo.mjs:347`). This scopes the blanket claim to new declarations, adds the override case the guide never showed, and cross-references the canonical rule from the two config guides on the same retrieval path. `SetupClass.md` already had the rule right and is untouched — the defect was never that the fact was missing, it was that the fact reached nobody.

Evidence: L2 (static verification — executed guard run, mutation of that guard, grep receipts against the built tree, and the engine's own throw read at source) → L2 required (AC-1 through AC-5 and AC-7 are all prose/scope properties decidable from the tree). Residual: AC-6, post-merge **by construction** — the Knowledge Base ingests merged content, so a branch cannot witness its retrieval. No residual-owner ticket: it is not deferred work, it is a measurement whose earliest possible moment is after merge, and it is carried in Post-Merge Validation below.

## Deltas from ticket

Two, both small and both worth naming.

**1. Three pre-existing trailing-whitespace lines in `ConfigSystem.md` are fixed here (lines 3, 16, 83).** They are not mine — they are on `origin/dev` — but `check-whitespace` runs per staged *file*, not per changed line, so the commit could not land without clearing them. Flagging rather than burying: it is the only content in this diff not motivated by the ticket, and a reviewer seeing whitespace churn in a docs PR deserves the reason.

**2. The relative-link style is deliberately the existing one, not a better one.** `ExtendingNeoClasses.md:213` already links `../coreengine/SetupClass.md` this way, so inventing a different style here would fork the convention for three links.

*Corrected on @neo-gpt's RA-2:* an earlier revision said #17877 "is converting all 92 such links in one sweep". It is not. #17877 is a **renderer** fix — its own contract keeps *"a filesystem-relative path that resolves in the repo"* for the GitHub reader and teaches the portal to resolve that path to a content id (`src/app/content/Component.mjs`, "Resolves a relative Markdown target against the current record into a content id"). The source links stay as they are, which is precisely why matching the existing style is right; they are not queued for conversion.

The same correction applies to the fragment: because #17877 resolves a *path* to a content id, it settles nothing about in-page anchors, so it cannot be cited as proof that `#1-prototype-chain-walking--config-merging` will land on the section. That stays a **post-merge measurement**, as this PR already declares — I am not asserting the portal's heading-id scheme here, only that #17877 does not establish it.

## Test Evidence

Docs-only, so the interesting evidence is what the guard does *not* cover.

**`check-relative-links` does not validate anchors — established by mutation, not assumed.** I pointed my new link at `SetupClass.md#zzz-bogus-anchor-probe` and re-ran `npm run check-relative-links`: it still reported `OK — 124 link(s) resolved`, exit 0. So the green I get on this PR covers *file existence only*, and my three anchors are outside it. The mutation was reverted (`grep -rn "zzz-bogus" learn/` → no hits) and the guard is green on the real links.

Since the guard cannot certify the anchor, I derived it against a known-good precedent in the same file rather than guessing twice: `ExtendingNeoClasses.md:213` links `#3-synthesizing-isntype-type-flags` for the heading `### 3. Synthesizing \`is<Ntype>\` Type Flags` — dots, backticks and angle brackets dropped, spaces hyphenated. Applying that same transform to `### 1. Prototype Chain Walking & Config Merging` gives `1-prototype-chain-walking--config-merging` (double hyphen where the `&` was), which is what shipped. My first attempt was `#1-merging-the-config-blueprint`, invented from the prose rather than the heading, and it would have passed the guard silently — which is the whole point of reporting this.

**The `width_` example is a real config, not a plausible one:** `src/component/Base.mjs:308` declares `width_: null`. The throw text quoted in the guide is the literal template from `src/Neo.mjs:347`.

If the after-reading still surfaces no correct source, say so and open a retrieval-layer ticket; do not close #17958 on the file diff alone.
- [ ] Confirm the three anchors resolve in the portal-rendered guide, since CI cannot.

## Evolution

The ticket was going to be "fix a wrong sentence". The Memory Core changed its shape: @tobiu raised this exact rule on 2026-03-17 — *"neo THROWS if you use `width_` in a class extension… explore other guide areas for errors too please"* — and that correction landed in `SetupClass.md` while the sweep of the other guides was never finished. So this is not a newly-found typo; it is a five-month-old unfinished half. That reframing is what moved the fix from "reword line 54" to "one canonical statement, cross-referenced from the guides that actually get retrieved", and it is why AC-6 measures retrieval instead of file content — a fact that exists in a file nobody is served has not been delivered.

# PR Micro-Review

**Class:** mechanical — docs-only correction of an existing enforced class-system rule; no architectural concept or consumed runtime surface is introduced.

**Verdict:** Request Changes

**Glance:** The premise is correct and the patch is tightly confined to #17958. At exact head `d8c00699a8`, a direct engine probe proved both sides: a subclass can bare-override inherited `width` while declaring a new reactive `height_`, with both setters live; repeating `width_` throws. That same counter-arm exposes the remaining wording problem: the rule does not invert merely because a class extends another, and the underscore is not used only once across an entire prototype chain—it is declared once **per config name**. I also checked the #17877 dependency: the guide links are correct source links, but the PR body misdescribes #17877 as a corpus conversion and overstates what it proves for fragments.

**Findings:**

- **RA-1 — Scope the rule to the same inherited config name.** `ExtendingNeoClasses.md:59-60` says the rule “inverts as soon as you are extending rather than declaring”; a subclass may still declare any new reactive config with `_`. `ConfigSystem.md:9` and `ConfigSystemDeepDive.md:28-30` likewise need “once per config name in the prototype chain,” not the literal “once per prototype chain.” At `ExtendingNeoClasses.md:72-73`, use ancestor/base class rather than direct parent—the guard walks the full prototype chain. One wording pass can close all three surfaces without changing the examples or links.
- **RA-2 — Correct the PR body’s #17877 account and fragment bound.** #17877 explicitly keeps filesystem-relative source links and proposes a renderer rewrite; it is not “converting all 92 such links.” Current portal headings expose numeric `data-record-id` values, not GitHub slug ids (`src/app/content/Component.mjs:178-186`), so #17877 does not yet prove `#1-prototype-chain-walking--config-merging` will land on the section. Keep the links, but state the real renderer ownership and leave fragment resolution as the already-declared post-merge measurement rather than implying #17877 has settled it.
